page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144 is a high-memory compute instance powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors built on x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 72 dedicated physical cores and 144 virtual CPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The memory subsystem delivers 1116 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 504 MB shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) are enabled. The configuration does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote persistent disks for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and high-speed data processing capabilities. The instance achieved top-tier rankings in multi-threaded benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 134,960.09 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 156,247.55. Memory bandwidth is substantial, reaching 533.18 GB/sec on large-block read operations and 205.98 GB/sec on writes. Furthermore, the instance handles in-memory transactional processing with top-tier efficiency, executing over 209 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining high token-throughput during CPU-based large language model prompt evaluations.

Given its large memory capacity, expansive L3 cache, and massive thread concurrency, the c4-highmem-144 is well suited for resource-dense environments. It is aligned with large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, big data analytics pipelines, and parallel compilation tasks. The primary operational tradeoff involves single-core execution speed, which benchmarks in the middle 50%, making this instance most cost-effective when running distributed or highly multithreaded systems that fully utilize its 144 virtual cores.
